title: Janus Nanoporous Metal–Phenolic Nanosheet Membranes for Highly Efficient Osmotic Energy Harvesting
abstract: ABSTRACT Osmotic energy, harvested by reverse electrodialysis, is a huge and promising renewable power source. However, the implementation still remains a longstanding bottleneck due to the lack of high‐efficiency membranes with both remarkable ionic conductivity and high permselectivity. Here, we report a new membrane constructed by Janus nanoporous metal–phenolic nanosheets (Janus MPNs), which overcomes the intrinsic trade‐off between ion permeability and selectivity. The Janus MPNs prepared via a facile interface‐induced coordination assembly strategy feature an asymmetric bilayer architecture comprising a microporous domain containing ∼0.96 nm pores and a mesoporous domain containing ∼9.4 nm pores, with each domain approximately 10 nm thick. The assembled Janus MPNs membrane integrates interlayer 2D nanofluidic pathways with ordered intralayer 1D nanochannels, enabling ultrafast ion transport rates approximately 21 times those of membranes relying solely on interlamellar transport. More importantly, the intrinsic sub‐nanometer pores and abundant negative surface charges within the metal–phenolic framework enable high cation selectivity, yielding a cation transference number ( t + ) of ∼0.936. When applied in reverse electrodialysis, the Janus MPNs membrane delivers a power density of 22.1 W m −2 under a simulated sea/river salinity gradient, outperforming state‐of‐the‐art two dimensional (2D)‐material‐based membranes. This work establishes new scaffolds for membrane technology and osmotic energy harvesting.

title: Maleimide‐Functionalized Conjugated Polymers Enable Covalent Biotic–Abiotic Integration to Boost Microbial Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Integrating advanced conductive materials into microbial electrosynthesis systems is a powerful paradigm for merging abiotic performance with biotic specificity, facilitating sustainable transformation of organic waste and carbon dioxide into value‐added chemicals. The regulation of biotic‐abiotic hybrid interfaces in biohybrids is crucial for improving surface microbial abundance, enhancing electron injection, and increasing electrosynthesis production. Herein, maleimide‐functionalized conjugated polymers (p(mNDI‐gT2)) were employed to construct robust, covalent bio‐interfaces via in situ click reactions with cytochrome thiol groups of Shewanella oneidensis , resulting in a doubling of bacterial adhesion. Moreover, intimate contact and binding interactions drastically reduce interfacial resistance and boost electron injection. As a direct consequence of this optimized architecture, the system achieved a 23‐fold increase in electron transfer and a 6‐fold improvement in electrochemical reduction relative to bare S. oneidensis . Furthermore, it obviously outperformed the non‐covalent group, yielding a 2‐fold enhancement in total charge output and a 2‐fold increase in succinate yield. Molecular docking simulations and proteomic analysis collectively reveal that p(mNDI‐gT2) not only facilitates efficient charge transfer but also predominantly upregulates the expression of key respiratory and bio‐interface protein complexes. Fundamentally, this covalent biotic–abiotic interface transcends traditional bulk‐adsorption methods, shifting the paradigm from simple microbial coating to molecular‐level interface engineering.

title: Hydrogen-bond-mediated quasi-two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks for ultrahigh gold extraction
abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are ideal for precious metal recovery due to their high surface areas and tunable binding sites. However, the confinement of binding sites within inner pores often leads to restricted mass transfer, resulting in poor site accessibility and limited extraction capacities. Herein, we report a quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) topology-directed strategy to construct exposed binding sites for highly efficient gold recovery. By incorporating outward-pointing hydroxyl groups, the local conformation of the imine-linked skeleton is effectively locked via inter-chain hydrogen bonding (ICHB), which suppresses molecular torsion and promotes ordered assembly of the 1D chains into a quasi-2D crystalline architecture. This structural rigidification creates unobstructed ion-diffusion pathways and maximizes the exposure of active sites for rapid [AuCl4]− capture and reduction. Remarkably, under mild thermal and vibratory stimulation, gold nanoparticles form in situ and aggregate, yielding a high gold extraction capacity of 5082.32 mg g−1. Theoretical calculations demonstrate that ICHB-induced structural planarization creates a cooperative coordination environment and optimizes the energetic landscape for dechlorination, synergistically promoting guest enrichment and interfacial gold reduction. This work establishes a new blueprint for creating COFs with exposed active sites via inter-chain assembly, offering a scalable approach to maximize site accessibility and electron transfer for selective gold capture. Covalent organic frameworks are ideal for precious metal recovery but the confinement of binding sites within inner pores often leads to restricted mass transfer and limits extraction capacities. Here, the authors report a quasi-2D topology-directed strategy to construct exposed binding sites for highly efficient gold recovery.

title: Electrochemically Driven Phenazine Autoxidation Coupled With Supported Liquid Membrane Technology for Hydrogen Peroxide Production
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrosynthesis offers a direct route to utilize clean electricity to create low–emission pathways for chemical manufacturing. For direct electrosynthesis of highly active compounds such as hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ), however, the close coupling of product formation and decomposition at electrode interfaces, together with energy intensive product–electrolyte separation, leads to energy losses and limited scalability. Here, we develop an electrified supported liquid membrane platform as a scalable and practical method for H 2 O 2 production as an important model compound. In this architecture, electrons from an external power source are temporarily stored in a designed organic mediator that is subsequently autoxidized within a physically segregated supported liquid membrane domain. This structural–decoupling strategy suppresses electrode driven decomposition, simplifies product handling, and permits independent tuning of electrochemical, transport, and product formation environments within a compact, modular device constructed from inexpensive components. The platform produces high–purity aqueous H 2 O 2 with Faradaic efficiencies up to 80%. We further demonstrate direct, on–site utilization of the generated oxidizing equivalents via in situ Fenton oxidation of an organic contaminant, thereby converting intermittent renewable electricity into localized water–treatment capability. More broadly, this strategy establishes an integrated and flexible reactor design framework for multiphase, electrochemically mediated synthetic processes beyond H 2 O 2 .

title: Precise modular engineering of neutral organometallic rectangles from binuclear palladacycles via hierarchical assembly strategy
abstract: Abstract Metallosupramolecular assembly provides a powerful strategy for the precise construction of well-defined architectures with diverse topologies and functionalities. However, the construction of neutral organometallic architectures supported by robust metal-carbon bonds remains underdeveloped, largely because kinetic persistence limits the reversible structural correction required for conventional self-assembly. Herein, we employ binuclear palladacycles as intrinsically neutral and geometrically preorganized building blocks and develop a hierarchical assembly strategy that temporally separates geometric programming, scaffold editing, and topology locking. Through a polymerization-cleavage-assembly process, cyclopalladated polymers are converted into discrete binuclear precursors while retaining their programmed geometrical information. Subsequent trans-effect-directed N -heterocyclic carbene ligation affords a series of size-tunable, kinetically robust, and neutral organometallic rectangles. The resulting architectures are fully characterized by spectroscopic methods and single crystal X-ray diffraction analyses. Moreover, single crystal X-ray diffraction identifies guest-mediated breathing-like geometric deformations in the solid state, driven by exo-wall π-π stacking and charge-transfer interactions with both electron-rich and electron-deficient planar guests. This work establishes a hierarchical construction principle for accessing discrete neutral organometallic architectures by separating geometric programming from the final locking of the topology through strong bond formation, while demonstrating that local geometric adaptation can occur without disrupting the framework connectivity established by Pd-C bonds.

title: Scalable Upcycling of Industrial Waste Polytetrafluoroethylene Into Porous Carbon Nanosheets by Zeolite Particle Templates for Capacitive Energy Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Upcycling highly stable polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) waste into value‐added carbon materials is fundamentally hindered by its complete zero‐residue pyrolysis, which exclusively emits hazardous fluorocarbons rather than forming solid carbon frameworks. Herein, we present a scalable zeolite‐particle‐templated cocarbonization strategy that catalytically transforms industrial PTFE waste into hierarchical porous carbon nanosheets (PCNs) while fixing over 81% of the fluorine as recyclable NaF. Comprehensive mechanistic investigations reveal that the ZSM‐5 template electronically activates C─F bonds and lowers the defluorination barrier, driving a successive‐condensation structural evolution. The resulting PCN, featuring an ultrahigh specific surface area and hierarchical porosity, delivers exceptional dual‐mode energy storage performances. In supercapacitors, PCNs achieve a remarkable specific capacitance of 429.6 F g −1 and outstanding rate capabilities driven by reversible pseudocapacitance and ion coadsorption. Concurrently, in carbon‐based aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (CAZBs), the PCNs deliver a high specific capacity of 267.0 mAh g −1 with robust extreme‐temperature adaptability (−25°C). Validated by a continuous industrial‐scale piping and instrumentation design (PID), this strategy demonstrates high commercial viability with low energy storage costs, pioneering a waste‐to‐wealth strategy for advanced carbon materials for energy storage.

title: Reprogramming Stereocontrol Through Progressive Substrate Reorganization in Artificial Triplet Photoenzymes
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise control of stereoselectivity remains a fundamental challenge in artificial enzymatic catalysis, particularly for artificial photoenzymes that lack evolutionary coupling between photosensitizer positioning and substrate recognition. Herein, by integrating crystallography, kinetics, molecular simulations, and protein engineering, we show that the enantioselectivity of an artificial triplet photoenzyme TPe4.0_FBpA for [2+2] cycloaddition originates from a highly organized indole substrate assembly within the photoactive cavity. Guided by these insights, progressive remodeling of substrate organization through minimal active‐site engineering reverses enantiopreference (from 99.5:0.5 e.r. to 2:98 e.r.) while preserving the sequence position of the genetically encoded photosensitizer. Structural and computational analyses further support a switch in the dominant stereocontrol mode from template‐assisted substrate organization to dispersion‐driven conformational confinement. These findings establish substrate organization as a programmable determinant of stereochemical outcome in artificial photoenzymes and provide a mechanistic framework for stereodivergent excited‐state biocatalysis.

title: Decoction-inspired thermo-mechanical coupling creates hierarchical nanohelix from herbal medicine for lipophagy therapy
abstract: Abstract Oral supramolecular nanomedicines often suffer from kinetic trapping, forming metastable aggregates with poor gastrointestinal stability and premature drug release. Conventional assembly methods rarely overcome these barriers. Inspired by the traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) decoction process, which intrinsically combines heating with mechanical stirring, we applied a thermo-mechanical coupling strategy to baicalin and berberine assemblies. Coupled thermal energy and fluid shear drove a transition from kinetically trapped metastable aggregate to thermodynamically stable left-handed nanohelix with an ordered crystalline lattice. This higher degree of structural order conferred improved gastrointestinal tolerance and extended the in vivo mean residence time to 23.06 ± 0.47 h. Sustained systemic exposure activated the AMPK–FoxO1–TFEB–lysosome axis, promoted hepatic lipophagy, and alleviated metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease in mice. These findings provide a physical chemistry framework for overcoming kinetic traps in supramolecular assembly, elucidate the nanoscale organization underlying traditional decoction, and offer a design strategy for long-acting oral nanotherapeutics.

title: Green Surfactant as a Soft Template for γ- Mesoporous Alumina Nanoparticles Preparation as Adsorbent and Carrier for Moxifloxacin Drug
abstract: The unique properties of nanomaterials, coupled with significant progress in nanotechnology, have driven a growing need for their manufacture. Additionally, because manufacturing processes generally result in increased pollution and environmental damage, there is a growing trend toward natural sources. In this study, a safe, environmentally friendly, and inexpensive natural surfactant was used as a soft template to synthesize mesoporous γ-alumina nanoparticles (γ-MNP). The template was the extracted solution of leaves of Zyziphus spina Christi, a widely available local plant, and aluminum nitrate as a precursor. The prepared γ-MNP was characterizing by using different analysis methods: FTIR, XRD, SAXRD, SEM, EDX, and AFM. Surface area was measured by the BET method, and porosity was measured by BJH. The prepared nanomaterials had a surface area (279.31 m2g-1), pore volume (0.572 cm3g-1) and pore diameter of 8.199 nm. The obtained BJH pore size distribution and average pore diameter and the hysteresis loops of the isotherms confirmed the mesoporous nature of the prepared sample. The XRD analysis shows that the sample is in a crystalline form with γ- phase and the SEM investigation shows that the sample appears to have nano-sized, smooth spherical, and high and regular agglomeration. The AFM histogram of granularity accumulation distribution shows that the particles range from 10 to 100 nm in composition (72%). The effectiveness of the manufactured γ-MNP as an adsorbent and carrier for moxifloxacin was tested.

title: Layered Precursor‐Guided Growth of Nondegenerate Amorphous In 2 O 3 Approaching the Thickness Limit
abstract: ABSTRACT Oxide semiconductors are promising channel materials for ultrathin electronics. However, conventional growth methods often produce excess carriers, poor stability, and interfacial issues, limiting their electronic applications. Here, we present a layered precursor‐guided synthesis of atom‐thin amorphous indium oxide (In 2 O 3 ) by oxidizing a layered InSe precursor within a back‐end‐of‐line (BEOL)‐compatible thermal budget. The oxide thickness is precisely controlled by the number of precursor layers, enabling In 2 O 3 as thin as 0.63 nm at the physical thickness limit. By avoiding localized nucleation and island coalescence issues, the resulting In 2 O 3 exhibits atomically smooth surfaces and excellent electrostatic uniformity with potential variations below 22 meV. Capacitance‐voltage analyses confirm a carrier density of 2.8 × 10 18 cm −3 in the nondegenerate regime and a low interface trap density of 10 10 ∼10 11 cm −2 ·eV −1 . We further demonstrate reproducible enhancement‐mode transistors with sub‐3 nm channels, featuring near‐zero threshold voltage, a low subthreshold swing (SS) of ∼74 mV/dec, a negligible hysteresis of < 10 mV, and robust gate‐stress stability. This work establishes a reliable route for integrating ultrathin, high‐performance amorphous oxide semiconductors, pushing the limits of next‐generation nanoelectronics.

title: Framework Deuteration Regulates Excited-State Dynamics and H2O2 Release in Covalent Organic Framework Photocatalysis
abstract: Abstract Hydrogen/deuterium (H/D) substitution provides a unique means of perturbing nuclear motion while largely preserving electronic structure. Here, we investigate isotope-regulated photocatalysis using structurally matched H-TpPa and D-TpPa covalent organic frameworks (COFs) for H2O2 production. Deuteration preserves framework connectivity, crystallinity, porosity, and ground-state electronic structure, yet increases the H2O2 production rate by 1.80-fold in O2-saturated pure water. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses show that D-TpPa exhibits weaker effective exciton–phonon coupling, a lower apparent exciton-dissociation energy, a longer-lived photoexcited population, and redistributed mode-resolved Huang–Rhys contributions, collectively improving charge utilization. Both isotopologues follow the same coupled two-electron oxygen reduction and four-electron water oxidation pathway. At the catalytic interface, isotope-dependent vibrational free-energy contributions reduce terminal *HOOH stabilization and lower the free-energy requirement for H2O2 release. These results establish framework isotope engineering as a generic strategy for regulating photocatalysis from excited-state evolution to interfacial product release without substantial electronic reconstruction.

title: Bio-Assisted Self-Activation of Porous Carbon in the Presence of Endogenous Silica for High-Performance Supercapacitors
abstract: Abstract In the pursuit of high-performance supercapacitors, it remains a key challenge to rationally engineer carbon electrodes with concurrently optimized porosity, surface chemistry, and structural integrity. In this work, a plant-mediated self-activation strategy is developed to construct hierarchically porous and nitrogen-doped carbon materials via endogenous nanosilica uptake. During plant growth, uniformly distributed SiO2 acts as both an in situ hard template and a catalytic promoter during carbonization, enabling the formation of a hierarchical pore structure without external activation. Meanwhile, SiO2-regulated nitrogen metabolism induces intrinsic nitrogen doping in the derived carbon framework, establishing a coupled biological-chemical pathway for heteroatom incorporation. The optimized SiO2-100@C delivers a high specific capacitance of 259.3 F g–1 at 0.5 A g–1 and retains 85% at 5.0 A g–1, together with excellent cycling stability of 95.53% after 20,000 cycles. The superior performance is attributed to synergistic effects of hierarchical porosity, enhanced ion transport, and regulated heteroatom configuration within a robust C-SiO2-derived framework. This work provides a sustainable and scalable strategy that integrates biological uptake with nanoscale structural engineering for advanced carbon-based energy storage materials.

title: Solvent‐Mediated Multi‐Factor Structural Modulation for Tunable Phosphorescence in Metal–Organic Frameworks
abstract: ABSTRACT Independently controlling phosphorescence dynamics while preserving the intrinsic emissive state is essential for establishing mechanistically clear framework‐phosphorescence relationships and rationally developing diverse phosphorescent metal–organic frameworks (MOFs). Yet conventional ligand/metal screening typically alters the emissive center. Herein, a novel solvent‐mediated multi‐factor structural modulation strategy yields five Zn‐based MOFs with tunable dimensionalities (1D, 2D, 3D) from a single metal/ligand system, exhibiting widely tunable phosphorescence lifetimes (12.6–1045.4 ms) and quantum yields (0.2%–16.2%), while retaining broadly similar ligand‐centered green emission, allowing kinetic differences to be attributed primarily to coupled structural variations. Single‐crystal structures reveal dimensional, terminal‐ligand, and guest‐confinement variations governing supramolecular interactions and framework rigidity. Theoretical analysis links these factors to distinct excited‐state localization, while γ/β descriptors link orbital mixing to intersystem crossing and radiative decay. Among the five structures, strong hydrogen bonding and guest confinement in the guest‐containing 2D MOF afford a 1045.4 ms lifetime, whereas semi‐chelate coordination and excited‐state localization in 1D MOF may favor a 16.2% quantum yield. These color‐stable, lifetime‐tunable materials enable covert exclusive‐OR optical encoding featuring parity‐check self‐validation and single‐bit error correction. This paradigm provides new chemical insights into decoupling phosphorescence dynamics from the intrinsic emissive state, enabling mechanistic elucidation and rational construction of multiscale, tailorable phosphorescent MOF systems.

title: Hierarchical Copper-Based Metal-Organic Frameworks for Improved Catalytic Performance
abstract: Introducing additional meso- or macroporosity into traditionally microporous metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) can greatly improve the catalytic performance of these materials, by reducing diffusional barriers during reactions. In this study, we demonstrate that HKUST-1 synthesized via supercritical CO2-assisted crystallization (referred to here as “scCO2-HKUST”) forms a hierarchically porous structure, combining intrinsic microporosity with newly formed macropores. X-ray diffraction (PXRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and gas sorption analyses confirmed the preservation of the crystal structure alongside macropore formation. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) revealed a higher proportion of low-valent copper species (Cuo/Cu+) in scCO₂-HKUST compared to conventional HKUST-1, indicative of increased coordinatively unsaturated metal sites. In catalytic CO oxidation, scCO2-HKUST achieved higher conversion rates than normal HKUST-1 between 220 and 260 oC, with complete CO conversion at 260 °C versus 280 °C for the conventional sample. This enhanced activity is attributed to faster molecular diffusion through the macropores and greater accessibility of reactive copper sites.

title: Interweaving Two‐Dimensional Co‐Corrole‐Based Covalent Organic Framework for Significantly Improved Electrocatalytic Oxygen Reduction Reaction
abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising electrocatalysts but suffer from limited active‐site accessibility, sluggish mass transportation in narrow‐spaced interlayers, and interlayer sliding during catalysis. Herein, we report the synthesis of Co‐corrole‐based 2D COF 1 and its interlayer‐interweaved derivatives 2 and 3 for electrocatalytic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). The reaction of Co tris(4‐formylphenyl)corrole and 1,4‐phenylenediamine gave 2D COF 1 with an interlayer spacing of 4.2 Å. Using pyrazine and bipyridine as bidentate molecular pillars to interweave 2D layers of 1 via bridging interlayer Co corroles, we obtained COFs 2 and 3 with interlayer spacing of 6.4 and 10.3 Å, respectively. Structural and spectroscopic analyses confirmed that the expanded interlayer spacing is caused by the axial Co–N coordination between Co corroles and bidentate molecular pillars. Compared to 1 , COFs 2 and 3 exhibited markedly enhanced 4H + /4e – ORR activity and durability, with half‐wave potential increased from 0.80 to 0.89 V and 0.94 V versus RHE. Rotation‐rate‐dependent Tafel measurements revealed improved mass transportation in the enlarged interlayer spaces in 2 and 3 . The Zn‐air battery using COF 3 delivered a high open‐circuit voltage of 1.52 V and a large peak power density of 193.5 Mw cm −2 , outperforming Pt/Ru benchmarks.

title: Engineering Steric‐Hindrance‐Guided Crystalline Vacancies in a Scalable Pillared‐Layer Nickel‐MOF for Efficient Gas Uptake and Separation
abstract: ABSTRACT Engineering local vacancies in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) presents a promising route to high‐performance gas adsorption/separation, yet conventional defect engineering often yields statistically distributed vacancies. Here, we report a steric‐hindrance‐programmed strategy to construct periodically ordered vacancies in pillared‐layer LIFM‐Ni‐3‐H 2 O via de novo synthesis by changing pyrazine linkers in a full‐pillared reference TJE‐1 to bulkier triethylenediamine ligands, resulting in missing‐pillars to produce potential vacancies in a regularly staggered interlayer fashion. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction unambiguously identifies the alternating pillar/vacancy arrangement, and digestion 1 H NMR supports overall stoichiometry. Removing capped water molecules converts LIFM‐Ni‐3‐H 2 O into LIFM‐Ni‐3 with complete exposure of the open‐metal Ni 2+ ‐sites, reshaping the local pore to form a contracted Window‐I and an enlarged Window‐II bearing open‐metal sites for molecular accessing and binding. LIFM‐Ni‐3 enables efficient separation processes: adsorbing SF 6 at Window‐II with 2.64 mmol g −1 uptake at 0.1 bar while excluding N 2 , and purifying CH 4 by removing minor C 2 H 6 /C 3 H 8 from natural gas with an exceptional productivity of 13.5 mmol g −1 . This represents a rare example that features simultaneously high capacity and selectivity by overcoming capacity–selectivity trade‐off, and combines favorable low‐pressure capture with fast apparent uptake responses. The scale‐up experiment testifies reliability of this pillar‐displacing approach for mass production and scalable gas separation.

title: High-order nanofluidic spiking encoding
abstract: Abstract High-order memristor is needed in neuromorphic engineering for sophisticated neural encoding. Progress has been made in solid-state memristor with electronic dynamics, which, however, presents a significant disparity with the ionic-chemical signaling in the human brain. Herein, we realize high-order nanofluidic spiking encoding based on synergizing the high porosity for non-linear ion transport, light responsibility for optical sensing, and catalytic chemistry for biological perception of a multifunctional covalent organic framework under nanoconfinement. The unique multimodal responses make possible the co-encoded spiking by electricity, light and real neurotransmitter glutamate in the physiological media, leading to the significantly enriched synaptic plasticity towards high-order spiking encoding behaviors, i.e. the rate encoding, time-to-first-spike encoding, rate and temporal fusion encoding, and history-dependent spiking encoding. It is expected to be a starting point for high-order nanofluidic spiking encoding.

title: Electrically Induced Photonic Assemblies of Faceted ZIF‐8 Crystals Exhibiting Binary Angle‐Dependent Structural Color and Metamerism
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrically tunable structural color has been pursued primarily in ordered photonic crystals (PhCs), where modulation of a sharp Bragg reflection provides an intuitive design handle. However, the dependence of observed color on viewing angles in PhCs limits their use for optical security and information encoding. Extending comparable electrical control to photonic glasses (PhGs), where multiple scattering pathways coexist and angle‐dependent coloration is suppressed, has remained less explored. Here, electrically driven photonic assemblies (PhAs) based on sub‐micron, faceted, zeolitic imidazolate framework‐8 (ZIF‐8) colloids are reported, exhibiting rapid and reversible optical switching under low applied voltages. Unlike conventional spherical colloids, the faceted geometry of the ZIF‐8 particles introduces pronounced angle‐dependent single‐particle scattering. Electric‐field‐induced assembly in liquid environments tunes particle packing and short‐range order, selectively reweighting the relative contributions of Bragg‐like reflection, diffuse scattering, and angle‐dependent single‐particle backscattering. This produces an unusual binary angular response, appearing blue at normal incidence and pink at oblique viewing angles. By designing a second assembly with indistinguishable normal‐incidence color but no angular switching, we further realize a metameric pair suitable to demonstrate two‐factor authentication. Spectroscopy measurements, combined with single‐particle scattering simulations, elucidate how electrically controlled particle packing and disorder govern optical response in metal–organic framework (MOF)‐based PhAs.

title: Metal–Organic Frameworks for Stabilizing Zinc Metal Anodes in Aqueous Batteries: Structure–Interface–Performance Relationships: A Critical Review
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (ZIBs), with intrinsic advantages such as environmental friendliness, cost‐effectiveness, and high theoretical capacity, have emerged as promising candidates for energy storage systems. However, the zinc anode in ZIBs faces several challenges, including dendrite formation, the hydrogen evolution reaction, corrosion, and surface passivation. These processes are strongly coupled rather than independent failure modes. To address these challenges, functional‐material‐based strategies involving electrode architecture, interface engineering, separator modification, and electrolyte regulation have been developed to improve the reversibility of the Zn metal anode. This review summarizes a structure–interface–performance framework for understanding MOF‐enabled stabilization of Zn metal anodes. Four implementation routes are systematically examined and compared: MOF protective coatings, MOF‐based three‐dimensional hosts, MOF‐modified separators, and MOF‐containing liquid, gel, or solid‐state electrolytes. Particular attention is paid to the relationships between pore aperture, framework chemistry, zincophilic sites, conductivity, mechanical integrity and five major interfacial functions: homogeneous nucleation, selective deposition, zincophilic regulation, accelerating Zn 2+ desolvation, and interfacial shielding against water and detrimental anions. Representative studies are critically assessed by considering the trade‐offs between ion selectivity and ionic conductivity, interfacial protection and transport resistance, and long‐duration laboratory cycling and practical Zn utilization, allowing to develop predictive design principles for MOF‐enabled aqueous Zn metal batteries.

title: Topological Carbon Quantum Rings With Near‐Unity Photoluminescence for Efficient Sky‐Blue Electroluminescence
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon quantum dots (CQDs) are promising environmentally benign emitters for next‐generation optoelectronic devices, yet aggregation‐caused quenching (ACQ) fundamentally limits their solid‐state emission efficiency. Existing strategies primarily rely on surface or morphological modifications, while the role of topology in regulating exciton behavior remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a topological design strategy to suppress ACQ by constructing carbon quantum rings with a closed‐loop conjugated architecture. Guided by symmetric molecular precursors, the ring formation process is elucidated by combined mass spectrometry and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, revealing a thermodynamically driven evolution from planar oligomers to curved and ultimately closed‐loop structures. This unique topology intrinsically suppresses intermolecular π–π coupling and non‐radiative decay, while enabling exciton confinement within a rigid conjugated framework. As a result, the carbon quantum rings exhibit a near‐unity photoluminescence quantum yield of 99.5% in solution and 58.9% in solid‐state films. When integrated into electroluminescent devices, efficient sky‐blue emission is achieved with a low turn‐on voltage of 2.8 V, a maximum luminance of 1020 cd m −2 , and an external quantum efficiency of 3.4%. This work establishes topology as a fundamental design parameter for carbon‐based emitters and provides a general strategy for overcoming ACQ in sustainable optoelectronic materials.

title: Blending With Insulating Polymers Enables Stable Anti‐Ambipolar Characteristics in n‐Type Organic Mixed‐Conductors for Heterogeneous Spiking Neurons
abstract: ABSTRACT Mammalian neurons exhibit diverse structural and physiological properties: a heterogeneity not present in current neuromorphic systems. Recent advancements have led to bio‐realistic spiking systems which are based on the integration and long‐term operation of organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) with anti‐ambipolar characteristics. However, the library of materials enabling anti‐ambipolarity (AA) is restricted by the lack of stable, fast, and scalable organic mixed ionic and electronic conductors (OMIECs) exhibiting this specific OFF‐ON‐OFF behavior. This complicates mimicking specialized neuron types. Blending semiconducting with insulating polymers is a classic organic and OMIEC electronics strategy to improve device performance and enable tunability, yet unexplored for improving anti‐ambipolar stability in non‐ladder‐type anti‐ambipolar materials. Here, the n‐type OMIEC, P(gNDI‐gT2), is blended with the insulating polymer, PMMA, yielding stable anti‐ambipolar characteristics. The miscibility in solution forms a mechanically stabilizing and ion‐permeable framework in the solid state that considerably reduces swelling‐induced structural damage, thus preventing dramatic failure after the first operation cycles without compromising the conductive polymer's electronic pathways. Modulating the polymer blend ratio enables low‐power, fast‐spiking Hodgkin–Huxley neurons with tunable and programmable dynamics, without optimized device geometries, demonstrating frequency deconvolution and reservoir computing. These two computing primitive building blocks are essential for designing efficient spiking neural networks.

title: Crystal Integrity Suppresses Bulk Trapping in Potassium Poly(Heptazine Imide) for Selective Polyester Photoreforming
abstract: ABSTRACT Bulk defects in organic semiconductor photocatalysts intercept photogenerated charges before interfacial reaction, constraining activity and selectivity. Here, seeded molten‐salt recrystallization yields potassium poly(heptazine imide) (PHI‐K) nanocrystals with reduced cyano content and enhanced lattice coherence for polyester photoreforming. Density functional theory and transient absorption spectroscopy identify cyano‐derived occupied states as bulk hole traps. Defect suppression preserves observable hole‐polaron absorption and extends the average exciton‐associated absorption decay time from 69.52 to 984.72 ps, consistent with reduced trap‐assisted carrier loss. Under air mass 1.5 global (AM 1.5G) irradiation, crystalline PHI‐K photoreforms alkaline‐pretreated poly(glycolic acid) and poly(lactic acid) into glyoxylic and pyruvic acids with respective target‐product carbon yields of 95.2% and 92.5%. Corresponding H 2 evolution rates reach 42.6 and 26.0 mmol g −1 h −1 , with apparent quantum yields of 50.8% and 30.1% at 400 nm, respectively. In situ infrared spectroscopy, isotope effects, and carrier kinetics support a pathway in which holes drive two‐electron oxidation of surface‐bound α‐hydroxy species while electrons reduce protons on Pt. These findings establish crystal integrity as an organic semiconductor materials principle that couples bulk charge retention to selective bond conversion in conjugated photocatalysts.

title: Hidden Structures and Unusual Fourth-Nearest-Neighbor Interactions Drive Atomic Ordering in Thermoelectric AgSbTe2
abstract: Abstract AgSbTe2 is a leading mid-temperature thermoelectric material, with several doped variants achieving a figure of merit (zT) &gt; 2. However, the microscopic mechanism by which dopants facilitate cation ordering for enhanced thermoelectric performance remains elusive. Here, we combine synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function analysis and machine-learned force field molecular dynamics simulations to investigate pristine AgSbTe2 and its highest-performing variant AgSb0.94Cd0.06Te2. Our analysis reveals ∼0.2 Å local rhombohedral distortions due to cation off-centering within the average rock-salt structure. Upon Cd doping, the fourth-nearest-neighbor (4NN) atom pair correlations are distinctly modified, evidencing the emergence of local cation ordering along &lt;100&gt;. We find that the unusually strong long-range interactions along &lt;100&gt; arising from multicenter p-bonding promote bonding coherence and drive 4NN cation ordering. By understanding how Cd reshapes 4NN correlations and bonding topology, we establish a direct link between local structural order, chemical bonding, and charge transport in AgSbTe2. Our insights offer a unified structural and chemical bonding-based framework for understanding dopant effects and guiding the rational design of next-generation AgSbTe2 thermoelectrics.

title: Waveguided, Self‐Sensing Sheath–Core Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fiber Actuators
abstract: ABSTRACT Soft actuators capable of operating in confined and hard‐to‐access environments, while providing integrated self‐sensing capabilities, are highly desired for next‐generation robotic systems. Here we report a waveguided sheath‐core optical fiber actuator consisting of a liquid crystal elastomer core encased in a conductive sheath of carbon nanotubes/carbon black. Near‐infrared light guided through the fiber actuator drives reversible contractions of up to 38% and enables a load‐bearing capacity of up to 320 times the actuator's own weight. Arrays of these fibers enable independent optical addressing of individual actuators, allowing programmable multimodal gripping in confined environments. The conductive sheath simultaneously serves as a strain sensor, providing real‐time monitoring of actuation states via changes in resistance. By integrating photothermal actuation and self‐sensing into a single fiber architecture, this work establishes a multifunctional platform for soft robotic systems operating in spatially confined environments.

title: The Effect of Hydrophilic Headgroup Chemistry on Peptoid‐Directed Mineralization of CaCO 3
abstract: ABSTRACT Engineered mineralization of calcium carbonate (CaCO 3 ) provides one strategy for CO 2 capture removal. Developing additives to accelerate the process or control resulting polymorphs would enhance underground reservoir security and advance development of CaCO 3 ‐based building materials. Peptoids — sequence‐specific poly‐N‐substituted glycines — have been shown to accelerate CaCO 3 nucleation and growth, select for metastable polymorphs, and induce unusual morphologies, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate control of these phenomena by using amphiphilic di‐block peptoids with carboxyl (‐COOH) and amine (‐NH 2 ) rich hydrophilic blocks. We demonstrate that ‐COOH‐functionalized peptoids free in solution drive rapid crystallization of calcite directly from amorphous precursors, bypassing the metastable vaterite phase observed in control experiments. Systematically increasing the number of ‐COOH groups progressively tunes calcite morphology from perfect rhombohedra to truncated structures to spindle‐shaped mesocrystals. In contrast, ‐NH 2 ‐bearing peptoids preferentially stabilize vaterite. When assembled into crystalline nanosheets exposing the hydrophilic block, only ‐COOH‐rich peptoid sheets nucleate crystals, unequivocally identifying carboxyl moieties as the key templating group for calcite formation. These findings provide chemical insights into controls of amphiphilic peptoids over CaCO 3 formation, establishing a platform for design of peptoids to control crystallization and advancing CO 2 sequestration and sustainable materials synthesis through carbonate mineralization.

title: Layer-by-layer water filling in molecular-scale capillaries monitored by AFM
abstract: Abstract Under ambient humidity, water spontaneously condenses in pores only a few nanometers in size, making nanoscale capillarity central to numerous natural phenomena and technological applications. At these dimensions, water may no longer be treated as a continuous fluid, yet the consequences of molecular discreteness for capillary condensation and filling remain poorly understood. Here we study two-dimensional (2D) nanocapillaries fabricated by van der Waals assembly and, using atomic force microscopy (AFM), monitor their wall deformations during humidity-driven water uptake. We observe two distinct regimes: layer-by-layer filling of flexible capillaries and abrupt filling of more rigid ones. Flexible walls deform in ≈3 Å steps, consistent with the entry of individual molecular layers of water. The different filling regimes are explained by a competition between wall deformation energy and oscillatory wall-water interactions. These results, together with the theoretical framework developed here, show how molecular discreteness can profoundly affect ubiquitous capillary phenomena, with wall rigidity determining whether this discreteness is exposed or hidden within an apparently classical, Kelvin-like response.

title: Thermally Induced Structural Transformation in a Two-Dimensional Conductive Metal-Organic Framework
abstract: A long-standing structural question in triphenylene-based conductive metal-organic frameworks is why closely related materials adopt either fully extended honeycomb lattices or intercalated structures containing alternating extended layers and discrete metal–ligand clusters. Ni(II)–HHTP and Co(II)–HHTP (HHTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene) have both been reported to have the latter “intercalated structure”, but here we discover that thermal activation and dehydration convert both frameworks to the fully extended structures. Focusing on Ni(II)–HHTP, we show that this structural transformation is reversible, with roomtemperature hydration restoring the intercalated structure. Variable-temperature synchrotron powder X-ray diffraction supports the intercalated-to-fully-extended structural transformation, while solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, thermal analysis, and elemental analysis provide evidence for the accompanying dehydration. Rehydration of Ni(II)–HHTP restores the intercalated structure, establishing reversible structural switching through removal and reincorporation of water. The resulting change in interlayer architecture alters electrical conductivity, gas response and adsorption properties in Ni(II)–HHTP. Importantly, common sample pre-treatment and testing conditions can themselves change the type of framework structure, meaning that measured properties may not correspond to the initially assigned structure. Because thermal and hydration history determine structure and function, careful structural verification under measurement conditions is, therefore, essential for establishing reliable structure–property relationships. Ultimately our findings resolve a persistent structural ambiguity in this family of materials and allow access to new fully extended electrically conductive framework materials.

title: A multimeric pore complex in the poxvirus core revealed by integrative structural analysis
abstract: Abstract It has long been known that poxviruses transcribe more than a hundred early mRNAs within their viral core, yet how these transcripts exit the core remains unknown. Here, we combine cryo-electron tomography with deep-learning-based particle picking, subtomogram averaging, cross-linking mass spectrometry, and AlphaFold3 modeling to resolve the molecular architecture of a long-sought pore within the poxvirus core. The pore is formed by a heteromeric assembly of the viral proteins E8, E6, and L3, which together create a hollow hexameric tube spanning both the core wall and the surface-exposed palisade layer. Within the pore channel, we observe a rod-like density consistent with the viral RNA helicase I8, which may contribute to the release of the newly synthesized viral mRNAs from the core. We further observe a state of the pore lacking the outer and basal rings under transcription conditions. Together, our findings identify the structure and dynamics of a candidate mRNA-release pore within the surface layer of a double-stranded DNA virus and suggest that it may form part of the poxvirus transcription machinery.

title: Structural basis for curvature generation and functional specialization in spirochete flagella
abstract: Abstract Spirochetes are spiral-shaped bacteria whose curved periplasmic flagella drive corkscrew-like motility through viscous environments. Despite their clinical importance, molecular mechanisms underlying flagellar assembly remain poorly understood. Here, we combine cryo–EM of flagellar filaments natively isolated from oral pathogen Treponema denticola , with proteomics and comparative genomics to characterise the molecular organisation. We resolve two filament types to sub-3 Å resolution: thin FlaB3-only cores, and thick filaments with a FlaB1/2 core asymmetrically decorated by a sheath comprising FlaA1/2/3 and lattice proteins FlaL1/2. We show sheath asymmetry imposes differential axial compaction on the FlaB1/2 core, generating convex and concave filament faces and establishing curvature. FlaB sequence and glycosylation differences at sheath–core interfaces correlate with selective incorporation into distinct filament types, supporting a mechanism for regulated filament architecture. Phylogenetic analysis reveals FlaL conservation across spirochete lineages, suggesting modular sheath lattices provide an adaptable mechanism for tuning flagellar mechanics across diverse pathogenic lifestyles.

title: Organic Iron Sulfur Framework With Electron Transfer Capacity Promotes Photosynthetic Carbon Fixation
abstract: Iron-sulfur clusters (ISCs) are crucial prosthetic groups in natural proteins that participate in vital electron transfer processes. Although various artificial ISCs with catalytic activity have been constructed, synthesizing stable ISCs under aerobic conditions remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a hydrothermal synthesis strategy to produce metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) containing discrete ISCs, bridging the gap between biological ISCs and conventional iron sulfide minerals. Using terephthalic acid (TPA) as the organic linker to encapsulate ISCs, we constructed MOF-like nanosheets termed Organic Iron-Sulfur Frameworks (OISF). Comprehensive characterization, including Mössbauer spectroscopy have confirmed the crystal structure of OISF containing [2Fe-2S] cores. The OISF exhibits robust electron transfer capability toward various acceptors, mediated by the dynamic formation of interlayer S─S bonds. Leveraging this property, OISF is combined with chloroplasts to enhance dark reactions in vitro and applied as a fertilizer to promote the growth of spinach in vivo, highlighting the potential of stable ISCs in biochemical and industrial applications.

title: Position‐Resolved Fluorescence Polarization Maps Segmental Rigidity in Block Copolymer Micelles in Aqueous and Biological Media
abstract: ABSTRACT Polymeric micelles are widely used as nanoscale compartments for delivery, sensing, and soft‐matter applications, yet their performance is governed not only by size and morphology but also by the local mobility of polymer segments within the assembly. Here, we describe a position‐resolved fluorescence polarization strategy to map apparent segmental rigidity within block copolymer micelles. By covalently installing the same dansyl fluorophore at defined positions along an amphiphilic block copolymer chain, we selectively label the hydrophobic core, core‐corona interface, and oligo(ethylene glycol) (OEG)‐rich corona of the micelles. The resulting fluorescence polarization profiles reveal a pronounced core‐to‐corona apparent rigidity gradient in water, distinguish block‐segregated micelles from compositionally matched random copolymer assemblies, and report micellar responses to temperature, cosolvent, and salt. This method further enables structural interrogation of polymer micelles in biologically relevant media, revealing the unexpected finding that biological serum exerts opposing effects on apparent chain rigidity in the micellar core and corona. Together, these results establish position‐resolved fluorescence polarization as a practical platform for linking block copolymer structure, self‐assembly, local chain dynamics, and biological stability, opening new opportunities to rationally design micelles with environment‐responsive mechanical properties.

title: Tunable microscale assembly with ultrasound vortex tweezers
abstract: Abstract Ultrasound tweezers provide a powerful approach for the contactless manipulation of microscale objects, yet achieving structurally simple platforms capable of tunable particle assembly remains challenging. Here we introduce ultrasound vortex tweezers based on a Fresnel-spiral diffraction grating (FSDG) that converts an incident ultrasonic plane wave into a vortex beam carrying orbital angular momentum. The passive grating structure enables the generation of ultrasound vortex fields with tunable topological charge, producing ring-shaped trapping regions with adjustable spatial scales. Operating at 10 MHz, the system provides improved spatial confinement compared with conventional low-frequency ultrasound tweezers. Using this platform, we demonstrate controllable self-rotation of individual microparticles, tunable aggregation of multiple particles, and core-shell encapsulation in bidisperse particle systems. The rotational speed of trapped particles shows an overall increasing trend with increasing vortex order, while the aggregation and encapsulation processes can be regulated through vortex order, driving voltage, and actuation time. These results establish ultrasound vortex tweezers as a compact and versatile strategy for tunable microscale assembly, offering new opportunities for high-precision ultrasound manipulation in materials engineering and biofabrication.

title: Cell Spreading-Enhanced Electron-Transfer Electrochemical Cytosensor Enabling Single-Cell Detection
abstract: Achieving single-cell detection with electrochemical cytosensors remains challenging, owing to a poor understanding of how electroactive redox probes generate measurable signals near large, insulating cells. Here, we validate a cell–electrode interfacial electron-transfer effect, in situ visualizing that the measurable current signal originating from redox probes located at the cell–electrode adjacent interface, rather than from those distributed on the cell surface. Notably, cell spreading enlarges this cell-adjacent interface, thereby enabling effective current amplification. Guided by this effect, we design an integrated cytosensor platform that combines a highly conductive lamellar reduced graphene oxide (RGO)/Ti3C2Tx electrode chip, which facilitates lamellipodia-driven cell spreading, with a high peroxidase-activity FeCN single-atom nanozyme. This platform exhibits a 7.6-fold signal enhancement over conventional chips and a detection limit of 0.03 cells mL−1, allowing a resolvable current response from a single cell on the 2 cm2 large-sized chip. Furthermore, it demonstrates potential feasibility for clinical detection of circulating tumor cells, achieving 96% specificity and 87% sensitivity across 55 blood samples in distinguishing cancer patients from healthy controls. This work establishes a cell spreading-enhanced electron-transfer paradigm and advances electrochemical cytosensing toward high-performance liquid biopsy applications. Electrochemical cytosensors have emerged as powerful tools for single-cell analysis, but generating robust signals from individual cells remains a major challenge. The authors uncover a cell-electrode interfacial electron-transfer effect, in which only redox probes at the cell-electrode interface contribute to measurable currents. Exploiting this mechanism, they develop a cell spreading-enhanced electron-transfer (SEET) cytosensor and apply it to circulating tumor cell detection in 55 patient samples, achieving 96% specificity and 87% sensitivity.

title: Engineering Topological Structures in Nematic Liquid Crystals for Functional Applications
abstract: Abstract Topological structures in nematic liquid crystals (LCs) emerge because of spontaneous symmetry breaking or geometric frustration under specific boundary conditions during the alignment of LC molecules. Historically, these topological structures have been regarded as defects that should be eliminated in the display industry. However, by precisely controlling the topological structures of LCs and utilizing the resulting elastic energy landscapes and physical anisotropy, they can be used not only to model other physical systems but also as functional materials. As a result, the topological structures of LCs have attracted significant attention in condensed matter physics, photonics, and materials science. This Review introduces the underlying principles of topological defects and solitons emerging in nematic and chiral nematic LC systems, comprehensively discussing engineering strategies for their precise manipulation. Building upon these foundations, a broad spectrum of innovative applications, such as colloidal self-assembly, soft actuators, tunable optical and photonic devices, and hardware security systems, have been highlighted. Finally, an outlook is provided for the realization of next-generation functional devices and active metamaterials.

title: Janus Oil–Water Separation Membranes: Synthesis Approaches, Multifunctional Progress and Prospective Challenges
abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid industrialization produces massive oily wastewater and frequent marine oil spills, severely damaging ecosystems and human health. Conventional oil–water separation membranes are restricted by single functions, low efficiency, and severe fouling, failing to cope with complex working environments. Featuring asymmetric wettability and multi‐functionality, Janus separation membranes create a new route for high‐efficiency, energy‐saving, and sustainable oil–water treatment. This review systematically summarizes advances in this underreviewed field. It first introduces the origin and development of the Janus concept, then discusses two dominant fabrication methods: layer‐by‐layer self‐assembly and asymmetric chemical functionalization, covering electrospinning, chemical etching, and surface modification, alongside each method's merits and drawbacks. Beyond basic separation, we overview integrated multifunctions including desalination, heavy metal capture, stimuli responsiveness, antibacterial, and self‐cleaning capacities. Critical bottlenecks concerning material stability, fabrication cost and scalable manufacturing are analyzed, followed by prospects of novel substrates, intelligent responsive membranes and eco‐friendly fabrication. This review delivers systematic theoretical guidance and technical references to boost structural optimization, separation performance, and real‐world engineering deployment of Janus oil–water separation membranes.

title: Electrochemistry‐Enabled Optical and Plasmonic Programmable Metasurfaces
abstract: ABSTRACT Organizing metallic nanoparticles (NPs) into well‐defined arrays enables the design of complex, collective plasmon responses. In periodic lattices with controlled spacing, the plasmon modes of individual NPs can couple with the diffraction modes of the arrays, giving rise to lattice‐plasmon resonances. By controlling the geometry of the NP arrangement, the optical, electromagnetic, and chemical properties of the system can be precisely engineered, opening pathways to advanced technologies in electronics, optics, sensing, and catalysis. However, achieving such architectures over large areas while maintaining precise control over composition and morphology remains challenging. Electrochemically fabricated metasurfaces offer a complementary bottom‐up alternative to top‐down patterning, providing direct control over material composition and morphology through low‐cost processing. This Perspective discusses how techniques such as templated electrodeposition, in situ redox patterning, and electrochemical growth and dissolution enable the formation of subwavelength architectures with tunable functionalities, typically associated with more complex fabrication routes. Despite notable advances, the link between electrochemical growth mechanisms and the design of functional optical and plasmonic arrays remains fragmented across the literature. This Perspective synthesizes these developments, clarifies the advantages and current limitations of electrochemical approaches, and outlines emerging opportunities for scalable, electrochemistry‐enabled design of functional metasurfaces.

title: Volumetric self-assembly of addressable DNA frames
abstract: The ability to organize distinct molecular components at prescribed positions throughout a three-dimensional volume remains a central challenge in programmable self-assembly. Although DNA nanotechnology has enabled both highly addressable structures and assemblies of considerable size, combining these capabilities is limited by the growing number of unintended interactions between components. Here, we develop a sequence-encoded strategy for the volumetric assembly of uniquely addressed DNA origami cubes. Each cube carries 24 programmable address codes that determine its position through cooperative interactions with neighboring cubes. We formulate address generation as a coding problem, derive its theoretical capacity and develop computational methods to identify and suppress incorrect multivalent binding configurations. Using this approach, we assemble a range of three-dimensional architectures, including a 6 × 6 × 6 cuboid that contains 216 unique cubes, spans 300 nm and is encoded by a single scaffold and 361 distinct oligonucleotides. We further demonstrate site-specific organization of 18-nm gold nanoparticles into prescribed three-dimensional patterns and use single-molecule DNA-PAINT to resolve spatially encoded features at the level of individual cubes. These results establish a framework for large-scale volumetric self-assembly in which molecular identity, spatial position and cargo placement can be independently programmed, providing a route toward aperiodic nanomaterials with designed three-dimensional organization.

title: Micro- and Nanofiber Technologies: Principles, Preparation Methods, and Characterization
abstract: Abstract The special geometrical and chemical properties of micro- and nanofibers lead to a structured arrangement of materials, resulting in better functioning during filtration, separation, adsorption, catalysis, and sensing. It presents an overview of different basic principles of micro- and nanofiber production. It gives comparative analysis of the methods employed including electrospinning, self-assembly, phase separation, template synthesis, drawing, centrifugal spinning, solution spinning, and melt spinning, discussing their influence on fibers morphology and their scale-up. The chapter introduces the main methods of characterization such as microscopy, image-based diameter analysis, spectroscopy, and diffraction. Moreover, it illustrates the importance of thermal analysis, mechanical tests, wettability testing in terms of its importance for fiber production. It also relates the impact of sustainability on microfiber technology development, outlining the key aspects such as solvent choice and recovery, energy efficiency, extent of throughput, green precursors, and recycling of fiber membranes.
